name: KY-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+18 partisan lean in a Republican-favorable environment
Massive GOP spending edge and Polymarket pricing the Democrat at 2%
Democratic nominee's negligible fundraising (~$94k) with no outside support
model.rationale: KY-04's R+18 lean and a favorable Republican environment make this an open seat that is nearly impossible for a Democrat to flip, and markets price the Republican at 97%. The Democrat's fundraising is minimal while GOP-aligned outside spending is in the millions, so the forecast sits near the district lean with a slight environment adjustment.
model.watch: A late scandal or unusual candidate-quality gap on the Republican side could tighten the race, but no such evidence exists.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Thomas Massie (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Kentucky's 4th District is an open seat after Thomas Massie lost renomination, and Republicans remain overwhelming favorites. The district carries an R+18 partisan lean, and the political environment this cycle favors the GOP, giving the Republican nominee a cushion of roughly 18 points on fundamentals alone.

Ed Gallrein has raised over $3.5 million with millions more in outside support, while Democrat Melissa Strange has raised under $100,000 and drawn no outside spending. Prediction markets put the Republican's win probability at 97%. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the race rests on fundamentals, all of which point the same direction.
